results.title: Apple Bets on iPhone as the Hub of Its Artificial Intelligence Future
results.description: Apple’s artificial intelligence strategy is increasingly being built around a device millions of users already carry every day—the iPhone. The message was reinforced by Apple Chief Executive Officer John Ternus during his first major keynote as CEO, where he outlined what he described as the ideal device for an AI-powered future before revealing that the company already has such a product. Speaking at Apple’s Surprise and Shine event on September 9, 2026, Ternus asked the audience to imagine designing an AI device from the ground up. Such a product, he said, would need an always-on internet connection, a sufficiently large display, high-quality cameras and microphones, long battery life and the ability to work seamlessly with other devices without requiring users to learn an entirely new system. The description sounded, at first, like a preview of a new Apple product. According to Bloomberg technology journalist Mark Gurman in his latest Power On newsletter, some people within Apple also believed the presentation was leading towards the unveiling of a new home-focused AI hub. Instead, Ternus turned the argument back towards the company's most familiar product. “In other words, you would arrive at something remarkably familiar, because there's no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone.” The statement reflects a broader shift in how Apple is positioning its smartphone. Rather than treating artificial intelligence as a feature added to the iPhone, the company increasingly appears to view the device as the central piece of an AI ecosystem that will eventually include glasses, earbuds and other connected hardware. Why the iPhone matters to Apple's AI strategy Apple's timing is significant. The company is facing growing competition from rivals developing AI-first hardware and services. OpenAI, for example, has been working with former Apple design chief Jony Ive on new AI hardware since 2025. Apple has yet to introduce a completely new mobile product capable of replacing the iPhone as the centre of its ecosystem. That makes the existing smartphone an important foundation for the company's next phase of AI development. Reports indicate that OpenAI's first dedicated device may not arrive before February 2027, with the product reportedly expected to resemble a smart speaker with a camera rather than a direct replacement for the smartphone. That leaves Apple with considerable time to develop its existing hardware-and-software ecosystem while positioning the iPhone as the device through which users interact with its AI services. Apple's own description of the iPhone 18 Pro reinforces that strategy, referring to the smartphone as an “intelligent personal hub” while emphasising privacy and security. Apple and Samsung are pursuing similar ideas Apple is not alone in attempting to make the smartphone the centre of an individual's AI experience. Samsung has taken a similar approach with the Galaxy S26 Ultra, while Google's Pixel range has increasingly incorporated Gemini features designed to work with users' personal information and broader digital activities. The competition, therefore, is no longer simply about which company has the most capable smartphone. It is increasingly about which ecosystem can make artificial intelligence useful across the devices people already use. Apple has one potentially significant advantage: distribution. If AI features are built directly into iPhones and enabled by default, Apple can put its technology in front of an enormous existing user base without requiring consumers to download a separate application or purchase a new category of hardware. That could give Apple an important route to mass adoption of its AI services, even as competitors continue developing dedicated AI devices. The technology behind Apple's AI hub The company's argument is not based entirely on marketing. Apple has designed its AI architecture so that some requests can be processed directly on an iPhone using a relatively small on-device model. More demanding tasks can then be transferred to Apple's Private Cloud Compute system. Private Cloud Compute uses Apple silicon-based servers to process more complex requests while being designed so that the company does not retain the user's request after processing. The approach gives the iPhone two important capabilities: it can handle AI tasks locally when possible while also having access to substantially greater computing resources when a request requires them. That combination helps explain why Apple can present the smartphone as an AI hub. The device already contains the processor, wireless connectivity, battery, cameras, microphones and display needed to serve as the central point of interaction. Other emerging devices, including smart glasses, do not yet have the same combination of capabilities or battery capacity. Apple's AI infrastructure has outside links There is, however, another part of Apple's AI strategy that has received less attention. Apple's June announcement confirmed that Private Cloud Compute would also extend onto Google Cloud. The company has also said its current Apple Foundation Models were developed using technologies associated with Gemini. The development illustrates the increasingly complicated nature of the AI race. Even as Apple, Google and other technology companies compete over AI products and platforms, their underlying infrastructure and technologies can overlap in unexpected ways. For consumers, the important issue is likely to be how effectively those technologies are integrated rather than where every individual AI computation takes place. Future Apple devices may depend on the iPhone The iPhone's role could become even more important as Apple introduces additional AI-enabled hardware. Smart glasses reportedly expected from Apple are designed to work with an iPhone, while camera-equipped AirPods are also expected to rely on the smartphone as part of their functionality. That means Apple's emerging device strategy appears less focused on replacing the iPhone than on extending its capabilities into other products. Rather than each device operating as an independent computer, the iPhone could serve as the central processor, communications link and personal-data gateway connecting the wider Apple ecosystem. For consumers hoping that a future pair of smart glasses might allow them to leave the iPhone behind, that transition may still be several years away. The bigger challenge is Siri Apple's hardware gives it a strong foundation, but the success of the strategy will ultimately depend on software. The company has been under pressure to improve Siri and make its AI capabilities competitive with products such as Google's Gemini. Earlier testing of Apple's AI assistant found it lagging behind Gemini in some areas, including reliability issues that caused the assistant to stop responding in the middle of a request. That leaves Apple with a paradox: it already has the physical device that could serve as the centre of an AI ecosystem, but its software must become capable enough to justify that role. Ternus's argument is therefore less about introducing an entirely new AI gadget and more about transforming an existing product into the foundation for a broader computing platform. The iPhone already has the connectivity, computing power, battery, sensors and ecosystem connections required for the job. The remaining question is whether Apple's AI software can make that hardware feel as indispensable for artificial intelligence as the company believes the device itself already is. For now, Apple's message is clear: the future of its AI strategy is not necessarily a new device sitting beside the iPhone. It may be the iPhone itself.

results.title: Crack emerges on newly-built Motihari bridge; flyover shuttering collapses on Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga highway in Bihar
results.description: Patna, Sep 21 (IANS) Two separate infrastructure-related incidents have raised concerns over construction safety and quality in Bihar, with a flyover shuttering collapsing on the Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga four-lane highway and cracks appearing on the approach road of a newly inaugurated bridge in East Champaran. A section of shuttering installed for an under-construction flyover on the Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga four-lane highway collapsed at Majhauli Chowk in Muzaffarpur district on Sunday night. The incident occurred around 10.45 p.m. under the Bochahan police station area while concrete casting work was underway. Heavy-duty shuttering had been installed for the construction of the flyover when a section suddenly gave way during the casting process. The collapse produced a loud noise and triggered panic in the area. Police and personnel from the construction agency reached the spot after receiving information and began clearing the fallen shuttering and debris from the road. No casualties have been reported in the incident. The collapse occurred late at night, when traffic and pedestrian movement at Majhauli Chowk were relatively limited. The location witnesses heavy traffic and pedestrian movement during the daytime, raising concerns about the potential consequences had the structure collapsed during peak traffic hours. The exact cause of the collapse has not yet been established. The construction agency is examining the incident, while questions have also been raised about the safety measures being followed during the ongoing construction work on National Highway-27. Meanwhile, cracks have reportedly appeared on the approach road of the Manjuraha-Hardiya bridge in East Champaran, only around 20 days after its inauguration. The bridge, constructed at a reported cost of approximately Rs 13 crore, is located at Berua Ghat between Manjuraha and Hardiya, near the East Champaran district headquarters. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the approximately 72-metre-long and 7.5-metre-wide RCC bridge on September 1. The project was intended to improve connectivity in the surrounding areas and facilitate easier movement towards the district headquarters. According to local residents, a crack measuring approximately 20 feet has appeared on the approach road. A portion of the road also appears to have subsided, raising concerns about the condition of the newly constructed infrastructure. Locals have questioned the quality of the construction work and demanded a technical enquiry into the cause of the cracking and subsidence. A patch-like repair has been carried out at the affected portion of the approach road. However, residents have questioned whether the repair will provide a permanent solution. --IANS ajk/rad

results.title: Tamil Nadu: Madurantakam bypoll candidates get extra security amid public protests
results.description: Chennai, Sep 21 (IANS) The Tamil Nadu police have tightened security for candidates of major political parties contesting the Madurantakam Assembly by-election after public opposition during campaign visits led to arguments and minor scuffles in some parts of the constituency. The by-election in Madurantakam constituency in Chengalpattu district is scheduled for October 6. With polling approaching, political parties have intensified their campaigns, while candidates and their supporters are travelling across villages to seek votes and mobilise public support. As the campaign gathers momentum, candidates have reportedly faced questions and protests from residents in several villages over unresolved local issues. In some places, heated arguments broke out between candidates and members of the public during door-to-door campaigning and street meetings. There were also instances of pushing and jostling after supporters accompanying the candidates intervened in disputes. Police fear that such confrontations could escalate into clashes between residents and party workers if adequate security arrangements are not maintained throughout the campaign period. After these incidents, police have provided additional protection to candidates representing the main political parties. Police are now assigning around 10 to 15 personnel each day to accompany prominent candidates during campaign visits, particularly in villages where public resentment or political tension has been reported. Police teams are also monitoring campaign routes and public meetings to prevent clashes and ensure that candidates can canvass without disruption. Officers have been instructed to intervene promptly if arguments develop between residents and political workers. Meanwhile, members of the public have alleged that flying squads deployed for the by-election are not conducting vehicle checks with seriousness. They claimed that no major seizure of unaccounted cash or large quantities of pamphlets, posters and banners linked to electoral violations had been reported so far. Residents said stricter surveillance was necessary as the possibility of illegal cash distribution could increase in the final stages of the campaign. They urged the police and election authorities to intensify vehicle inspections, particularly on roads connecting villages and at entry points to the constituency. The public also sought round-the-clock monitoring of suspicious vehicle movements and stronger enforcement of election rules. Election officials are expected to step up checks as polling day draws closer, while police continue to assess security requirements based on the situation in each campaign area. --IANS aal/skp

results.title: Asha Negi on growing up in Uttarakhand: Heard so many stories about devi-devtas, supernatural happenings
results.description: Mumbai, Sep 21 (IANS) Actress Asha Negi, who hails from Uttarakhand, talked about how growing up in a state rich in folklore and supernatural tales shaped her fascination with the horror genre. While speaking to IANS, Asha recalled stories she heard from her family and a deeply overwhelming incident involving a village ‘jaagar’. She said she “definitely” believes in such supernatural experiences. Talking about how hailing from Uttarakhand, a state steeped in folklore and stories of the supernatural, has shape her fascination with the horror genre “I’ve heard a lot about ‘devi-devtas.’ In fact, when we went to Orchha for the shoot of Ali Baba, everyone was sharing their stories with the director. I remember telling them about an incident that happened in my family, back in our village,” Asha told IANS. She added: “We have ‘jaagars’ in our village, where a lot of prayers and rituals take place. Sometimes, during these rituals, it is believed that the soul of someone who has passed away from the family can also communicate or speak.” Jaagar is a traditional form of spiritual folk singing and ritual from the Kumaon and Garhwal regions of Uttarakhand. It is meant to invoke and "awaken" deities and ancestral spirits. Recalling an incident from her family, she said: “ This actually happened in my family, and it was a very overwhelming experience. I definitely believe in this, and these things do happen in our village. My parents would also tell me stories from the time when they used to live in the village. So, I’ve grown up hearing many such stories.” Asha’s latest show is “Ali Baba Aur 40 Bhoot”. The upcoming horror-comedy series brings together ancient folklore, haunted mysteries and adventure. The show also features stars Asha Negi as Ali and Vishal Vashishtha as Baba. Set against the mysterious world of Central Indian folklore, “Ali Baba Aur 40 Bhoot” follows Alisha “Ali” Nigam, a sharp, science-driven neuropsychology expert, whose search for her missing father pulls her into a world of supernatural mysteries. Asked if 40 “bhoots” represented 40 fears, which human fear is the most universal, Asha told IANS: “The most universal fear could be, ‘What do people think about me?’ Every person thinks about how others perceive them. I hope they think good things about me.” The 40-episode series premiered on September 11 on JioHotstar. --IANS dc/
